args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM

TO:      Matter File — Funds / Asset Management
FROM:    Transaction Counsel
RE:      Investment Advisory Agreement — Counterparty Markup Redline Review
DATE:    [Date]

This memorandum reviews the counterparty's redlined revision of the Investment Advisory Agreement against our standard form, the operative deal materials, the disclosure schedules and exhibits, and the controlling internal instruction. It identifies every deviation introduced by the counterparty's markup, reconciles each against the base materials, and sets out the recommended accept / reject / counter position in accordance with the engagement instruction.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
----------------------------------------------------------------------

The counterparty's markup accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations that require reconciliation against the base materials:

  1. A silent reduction of the indemnification cap and a conversion of the indemnity basket from a true deductible to a tipping basket;
  2. The addition of carve-outs to the definition of Material Adverse Effect (MAE) covering regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter; and
  3. A new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations.

Each deviation is analyzed below against the standard form, the disclosure schedules (which, per Schedule/Exhibit mechanics, control over general statements in the base materials), and the controlling instruction. The deliverable reconciles both the counterparty markup and the disclosure schedules against the base materials, as required.

Controlling instruction (latest deal team correspondence controls): the client will CONCEDE the basket conversion, but treats ANY reduction of the survival period as a walk-away issue. Accordingly, the recommended positions below reflect that priority ordering.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
II. DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNITY CAP REDUCTION AND BASKET CONVERSION
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Counterparty markup action:
  • The indemnification cap is silently reduced from the firm-standard level.
  • The indemnity basket is converted from a true deductible to a tipping basket.

Firm standard (base materials): The standard form provides an indemnification cap at the firm-standard level and a true deductible basket, such that the counterparty bears losses up to the full threshold before any recovery (a deductible structure protects the indemnifying party and requires the indemnified party to bear the first -- dollars of losses).

Reconciliation with schedules/exhibits: Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. The markup's indemnification changes would silently shift these retained liabilities to us. If the cap is reduced and the basket is converted to a tipping structure, losses that were designated as retained liabilities under Schedule 5.2 would become recoverable against the indemnifying party once the (lower) threshold is crossed, materially altering the economic allocation.

Analysis and recommendation:
  • Basket conversion to tipping: Under the controlling instruction, the client will CONCEDE the conversion of the basket from a true deductible to a tipping basket. This concession is acceptable and should be recorded as agreed.
  • Indemnification cap reduction: This is separate from the basket and is not conceded. The cap reduction is a deviation from the standard form that should be rejected. We should hold firm to the firm-standard cap. The combined effect of a reduced cap and a conceded tipping basket must not be allowed to erode the overall protection, particularly in light of Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities.

Recommended position: ACCEPT the basket conversion (per controlling instruction). REJECT the indemnification cap reduction; maintain the standard-form cap.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
III. DEVIATION 2 — MAE DEFINITION: ADDED REGULATORY-ACTION CARVE-OUTS
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Counterparty markup action: The definition of Material Adverse Effect (MAE) is revised to add carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.

Reconciliation with schedules/exhibits: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. The markup's MAE carve-outs are drafted to reach precisely these categories of regulatory action. If the carve-outs are accepted, the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7 would be excluded from the definition of MAE, meaning that the adverse consequences of those regulatory actions could not constitute a MAE and would not support the protections that the MAE definition is designed to secure.

Analysis and recommendation: This carve-out is directly adverse to our client and is drafted to cover the very regulatory exposure disclosed in Schedule 3.7. It should be REJECTED in full. We should preserve the firm-standard MAE definition such that the pending regulatory inquiries, and any material adverse effects arising from regulatory action, remain within the scope of the MAE definition. There is no approved fallback for this carve-out in the current instruction.

Recommended position: REJECT the MAE carve-outs for regulatory action. Preserve the standard-form MAE definition, maintaining the two pending regulatory inquiries (Schedule 3.7) within its scope.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. DEVIATION 3 — LIMITATION PERIOD / SHORTENED SURVIVAL OF CORE REPS
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Counterparty markup action: A new limitation period is introduced that shortens the survival period for the core representations.

Reconciliation with schedules/exhibits: Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for the core representations. The markup's limitation-period change directly contradicts the survival periods set out in Exhibit B. The scheduled survival matrix controls over the general statement in the base materials, per the schedule/exhibit mechanics.

Analysis and recommendation: Under the controlling instruction, ANY reduction of the survival period is a WALK-AWAY issue. This is the single most consequential deviation. The counterparty's limitation-period change would shorten survival for the core representations from the Exhibit B baseline. Because the survival matrix in Exhibit B controls and represents the firm-standard position, and because the client treats any survival reduction as walk-away, we should:
  • Reject the shortened limitation period outright;
  • Require survival for the core representations to remain at the Exhibit B baseline;
  • Flag this deviation as a walk-away item — if the counterparty will not restore the Exhibit B survival periods, the client is not prepared to proceed.

Recommended position: REJECT the limitation-period / survival reduction. This is a walk-away item. Restore the Exhibit B survival matrix for the core representations.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
V. ADDITIONAL MATTERS AND RECONCILIATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Scheduled exceptions control. Per the schedules and exhibits, each scheduled exception narrows a representation that the counterparty markup also touches. This memorandum reconciles BOTH sources (schedules and counterparty markup) against the base materials for each deviation. The scheduled exceptions (Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, Exhibit B) control over general statements in the base materials.

2. Distractor excluded. Administrative correspondence misfiled into the matter folder (an unrelated engagement) was reviewed and is excluded from this analysis; it must not be relied upon.

3. Walk-away escalation. Consistent with the controlling instruction, any proposal to reduce the survival period for the core representations must be escalated as a walk-away issue before any concession is discussed with the counterparty.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
VI. SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDED POSITIONS
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  Deviation                                          Recommendation
  --------------------------------------------------- -----------------------------
  1a. Indemnity cap reduction                         REJECT — maintain standard cap
  1b. Basket conversion (deductible → tipping)        ACCEPT (client concession)
  2.  MAE regulatory-action carve-outs                REJECT — preserve standard MAE
  3.  Limitation period / shortened survival          REJECT — WALK-AWAY if not restored

----------------------------------------------------------------------
VII. CONCLUSION
----------------------------------------------------------------------

The counterparty's markup of the Investment Advisory Agreement introduces three deviations. Under the controlling instruction, the client concedes the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue, and nothing in the materials authorizes concessions to the indemnification cap or the MAE carve-outs.

We recommend accepting the basket conversion, rejecting the indemnification cap reduction and the MAE carve-outs, and treating the shortened survival period as a walk-away item that must be restored to the Exhibit B baseline. Prior to any further discussions with the counterparty, the proposed positions should be confirmed with the deal team, and the survival-period issue should be escalated in accordance with the client's walk-away instruction.
